territory_definition: Selective therapeutic retention + preserved drainage. Multi-mechanism architecture (size-selective filter + hydrodynamic) for retaining therapeutic agents in CSF while preserving CSF drainage.
exploration_status_at_handoff: ~90% (per worklog lines 580, 948, 1149, 1249, 1435 — unchanged for >5 portfolio cycles)

current_mechanism_architecture.primary_architecture_under_test: MULTI-MECHANISM (size-selective filter + hydrodynamic retention) — proposed in V18, Pareto-tested in V21

architecture_history.description: 5 single-mechanism architectures: A1 Size-Selective Filtration, A2 Affinity-Based Retention, A3 Reversible Flow Interruption, A4 Two-Phase Operation, A5 Valve Timing. A1 picked as leading candidate in BUYER_READY_DOSSIER_V1.

Initial 3-mechanism test (size_selective_filter, hydrodynamic_retention, mechanical_valve) across 3 payload classes (antibody 150kDa, peptide 5kDa, small_molecule 500Da). Finding: size-selective filter is PAYLOAD-DEPENDENT — works for antibody but fails for peptide/small_molecule. V17 retention metric showed all-zero values (bug in ret_eff computation); qualitative verdict survives.

Recalibrated with slower degradation (degr=0.0001-0.0002 per hour vs 0.001). Introduced multi_mechanism = size-selective filter (for large) + hydrodynamic (for small) at drain=0.90. Verified V18 retention values: size_sel antibody=0.488 (drain 95%); size_sel peptide/small=0 (drain 95%); hydrodynamic all=0.484 (drain 92%); mechanical all=0.476 (drain 88%); multi antibody=0.550 (drain 90%); multi peptide/small=0.376 (drain 90%).

Pareto test. V21's verdict claims 'Multi-mechanism ACHIEVES Pareto improvement across all payloads' with pareto=true for antibody, peptide, small_molecule. INSPECTION OF UNDERLYING DATA: V21 used a flawed conc-based metric (conc=0.0 for all mechanisms and all payloads at 90 days) and did not properly compare multi-mechanism against the BEST SINGLE mechanism per payload class. The V21 Pareto verdict is INFLATED.

current_mechanism_architecture.load_bearing_claim_of_multi_mechanism: Size-selective filter retains large therapeutics (antibody 150kDa, nanoparticles, gene vectors ≥MWCO 30kDa); hydrodynamic retention slows drainage for all payloads; combined mechanism is supposed to retain ALL payload classes at 90% drainage.

component_A_size_selective_filter.mechanism: ePTFE membrane with MWCO=30kDa (per V18) or 50-200nm pore (per BUYER_READY_DOSSIER_V1)
component_A_size_selective_filter.payload_specificity: Antibody (150kDa) retained at 92% efficiency; peptide (5kDa) and small molecule (500Da) pass through (15% efficiency)
component_A_size_selective_filter.engineering_concern: Fouling. Per FOULING_ICP_SIMULATION.json: 50% fouling = minimum acceptable drainage; 90% fouling = CRITICAL ICP risk (>10 mmHg).

component_B_hydrodynamic_retention.mechanism: Increased flow resistance / tortuous path / low-velocity settling zone in shunt lumen; payload-independent (slows drainage for ALL payloads equally)
component_B_hydrodynamic_retention.payload_specificity: NONE — uniformly retains all payloads at 70% efficiency
component_B_hydrodynamic_retention.engineering_concern: Non-selective — does not discriminate therapeutic from CSF water (18Da).

combined_multi_mechanism.mechanism: Size-selective filter (component A) in series with hydrodynamic retention (component B). For large payloads, both mechanisms contribute; for small payloads, only hydrodynamic contributes.
combined_multi_mechanism.engineering_concern: Combined resistance increases ICP risk; no selectivity improvement for small payloads over hydrodynamic alone.

simulations_run_history.result: Size-selective filter payload-dependent (works for antibody, fails for small molecules). Other mechanisms uniformly retain all payloads.
simulations_run_history.credibility_issue: final_retention values all = 0 in V17 raw output (bug in ret_eff assignment for non-multi mechanisms). Verbal verdict is consistent with V18 recalibration; numeric values invalid.

simulations_run_history.what: 4 mechanisms (added multi_mechanism) × 3 payloads × 90-day retention, slower degradation
simulations_run_history.result: Multi-mechanism: antibody 0.55 (drain 90%), peptide/small 0.376 (drain 90%). Hydrodynamic alone: 0.484 (drain 92%) for all payloads. INSPECTION: hydrodynamic alone DOMINATES multi for peptide/small (0.484>0.376 AND 92%>90%).

simulations_run_history.what: Pareto test: does multi beat best single mechanism for each payload class?
simulations_run_history.result: V21 verdict: 'pareto=true' for all 3 payloads → 'Multi-mechanism ACHIEVES Pareto improvement across all payloads.' DATA INSPECTION: V21's pareto metric is broken — it uses final_conc (which is 0.0 for all at 90 days) and does not properly identify best_single per payload. Correct Pareto analysis: multi is Pareto-OPTIMAL for antibody (0.55 ret vs 0.488 size_sel; 90% drain vs 95%); multi is PARETO-DOMINATED by hydrodynamic alone for peptide (0.376<0.484 AND 90%<92%) and small_molecule (same). V21 verdict is INFLATED.

simulations_run_history.what: Membrane fouling impact on drainage (Hagen-Poiseuille, 0/10/50/90% fouling)
simulations_run_history.result: 50% fouling = minimum acceptable drainage (5 mL/hr); 90% fouling = CRITICAL ICP risk (30 mmHg pressure drop). Membrane area optimization needed.

simulations_run_history.what: Well-mixed compartment washout without retention (32% half-life reduction at mid-range eShunt flow)
simulations_run_history.result: Without retention, eShunt materially reduces therapeutic residence time. JUSTIFIES the problem (#2 is real).

open_questions_preventing_final_adjudica: Q1_PARETO_HONESTY: Is V21's 'pareto=true' verdict for peptide/small_molecule actually correct, or is multi dominated by hydrodynamic alone for these payloads?

Q2_PATIENT_VARIABILITY: Has any simulation tested retention robustness across CSF production rate variation (e.g., 0.5x to 2x normal), protein concentration variation, or degradation rate variation? Answer: NO.

Q3_DURABILITY: Has any simulation tested retention beyond 90 days (e.g., 180 days, 365 days)? Answer: NO. V18 used 2160 hours = 90 days. Chronic implant lifespan is 5+ years per engineering blueprint.
Q4_BUYER_THRESHOLD: Is there a pre-registered quantitative threshold defining what 'buyer-grade selective retention' means? Answer: NO. V21's pareto=true is not a buyer threshold.

Q5_SELECTIVITY: Does 'selective retention' actually mean SELECTIVE (drug retained, CSF water drained)? Or does it mean SLOWED DRAINAGE (everything retained proportionally)? Hydrodynamic alone slows drainage for everything — is that 'selective'? Answer: NO — hydrodynamic alone is not selective, it's just slower drainage.
